parakeet: I remember one of the first times doubt truly gripped me. I was preparing to preach, wrestling quietly in my study with contradictions and questions that I could no longer ignore. My heart raced, and I could feel the weight of every sermon I'd ever given pressing down on me. At that moment, doubt felt like betrayal, like I was failing myself, my community, even my God. But then something shifted. Instead of pushing those thoughts away, I sat with them. I allowed myself to ask questions I'd always feared asking. What if I'm wrong? What if the answers I've accepted aren't actually true? And most importantly, why am I afraid of these questions? Gradually, something incredible happened. Doubt didn't destroy me. It empowered me. It gave me permission to look honestly at what I believed and why. Rather than losing myself, I began finding a deeper sense of authenticity and self awareness. For the first time, I was living from a place of genuine curiosity rather than scripted certainty. Doubt doesn't weaken you. It strengthens your capacity for critical thought, empathy, and personal authenticity. It's a necessary and courageous step toward discovering a life defined by integrity rather than imposed beliefs. What doubts have you feared exploring and why? How could embracing your questions lead to greater authenticity in your own life?
